thread:
rachel: Starting thread for a short design sync: propose 'windowed local shaper' at edge proxies to smooth tenant bursts while keeping central quota authoritative. Idea: proxies enforce a per-tenant moving window allowance (tokens per 10s) instead of fixed instant credits. PTAL.

marta: moving window sounds promising. How do we compute allowance and avoid cross-proxy hoarding?

rachel: compute allowance = min(global_per_proxy_cap, floor(tenant_share * window_budget)). Central computes tenant_share and pushes every 5s; proxies apply decay to counts in sliding window.

samir: tradeoffs? windows longer -> smoother but slower reaction to abuse. shorter -> more central hits. Also need to handle skewed topologies where many clients hit same proxy.

rachel: mitigations: 1) cap per-proxy exposure, 2) cross-proxy reconciliation via periodic probes (sampled), 3) emergency clamp when central signals negative balance.

anya: what counts against the window? all admits that reach runtime. cache-only responses excluded. We should have runtime emit served=true/false to proxy.

dmitri: implementation note: sliding-window via fixed buckets (e.g., 10 buckets for 10s window) is cheap. We store per-key ring buffer counters; eviction LRU for low-volume tenants.

rachel: sample config: 

```
shaper:
  window_seconds: 10
  buckets: 10
  global_per_proxy_cap: 400
  heartbeat_interval_s: 5
  clamp_duration_s: 30
```

samir: observability: metrics needed: window_used_ratio, clamp_events, cross_proxy_skew, reconcile_latency. Also emit `X-RW-Shaper: clamp` header when denying.

marta: what about fairness across models and costs? make shard key tenant+model and weight tokens by model_cost.

anya: failure modes? proxy clocks skew will affect sliding windows. Use monotonic counters and rely on central heartbeat to correct drift. Also auth HMAC on heartbeats.

rachel: TL;DR: windowed local shaper reduces tail by smoothing bursts at edge; downside is complexity and potential temporary skew. Next: I'll draft a short RFC with failure modes, test matrix (Zipf workloads + partial central outage), and canary plan. Anyone volunteer to review?

samir: +1, i'll review telemetry section.

marta: I'll own the canary SLOs.

telemetrybot: NOTE: created dashboard template 'edge-shaper/overview' with base panels for window_used_ratio and clamp_events.

rachel: thanks all, will write RFC today and ping reviewers.
